after: ## Geographic themes -- seven options (60 hours SL / 90 hours HL)
alt: The seven options are freshwater; oceans and coastal margins; extreme environments; geophysical hazards; leisure, tourism and sport; food and health; and urban environments. SL classes study two (60 hours) and HL classes three (90 hours), chosen by the teacher.
caption: Revise only the options your class actually studied.

after: ## HL extension only -- Geographic perspectives: global interactions (60 hours, HL only)
alt: Two stacked bars. SL, 150 hours: options 60, core 70, fieldwork 20. HL, 240 hours: options 90, core 70, HL extension 60, fieldwork 20.
caption: HL adds a third option and a whole 60-hour extension.

alt: The chosen options are examined in Paper 1, the shared core on global change in Paper 2, and the HL extension on global interactions in Paper 3, which only HL students sit. Fieldwork is the internal assessment. A note advises building a bank of one or two specific case studies per theme.
caption: Know which paper tests which content before you start revising.

after: ## Internal assessment -- fieldwork (20 hours, both SL and HL)
alt: Four steps: choose a suitable topic from an option, the core or the HL extension; settle a testable question and realistic method before the trip; collect and analyse the information with evaluation; and evaluate the limitations of your own method. A warning advises against collecting data first and fitting a question afterwards.
caption: A testable question chosen early makes a stronger fieldwork report.
